name: King of Moab
overview: The King of Moab was a male monarch who ruled Moab during the reign of King Zedekiah of Judah, as noted in the book of Jeremiah. Beyond his role as king in this specific historical context, Scripture provides no additional personal details or tribal affiliations about him.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Moab' simply identifies this individual as the reigning monarch over the nation of Moab. The meaning of the title is straightforward, indicating his position of authority without further personal names or divine attribution.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or personal connections for the King of Moab beyond his status as king during Zedekiah's reign.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Moab's significance lies in his political role during a critical period in Judah's history under King Zedekiah. His mention in Jeremiah 27:3 situates him among the regional rulers involved in the geopolitical dynamics surrounding Judah at that time, highlighting the broader context of God's dealings with nations through prophetic messages.
